name: Cryogenic L-band (1.2-1.8 GHz) receiver front end for FAST: OMT at 55 K and Coupling-LNAs at 15 K in a GM-cooled rectangular dewar at 1e-5 Pa behind a film vacuum window
plain_name: Cool a giant radio telescope's 1.2-1.8 GHz receiver electronics to 15 K to cut its noise
description: The FAST single-beam L-band receiver: a 728.3 mm long conical quad-ridge OMT (189 mm internal aperture) is cooled by the first GM stage to ~55 K and two Coupling-LNAs (noise ~4 K) by the second stage to 15 K inside a rectangular vacuum dewar reaching 1e-5 Pa; the RF enters through a polyimide/Teflon film window. LNA noise at 15 K is measured with the Variable Load Temperature method and the receiver noise (<9 K) with hot/cold loads.
keywords: Cool a giant radio telescope's 1.2-1.8 GHz receiver electronics to 15 K to cut its noise

sources.citation: H.-F. Liu, C. He, J. Wang et al., 'Ultra-Low Noise L-Band Cryogenic Astronomical Receiver for FAST Telescope', Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics (2021), arXiv:2103.10677

reported_equipment: FAST L-band receiver rectangular cryogenic dewar
two-stage GM cold head and helium compressor

requirements.rationale: The Coupling-LNAs must operate at a physical temperature of 15 K.
The dewar reaches a vacuum of 1e-5 Pa to suppress gas conduction and convection to the cold parts.
The OMT and LNAs sit inside a vacuum dewar.
The sky signal enters the dewar through a large film vacuum window in front of the OMT.
The 728.3 mm long OMT must fit inside the cold space.
The OMT has a 189 mm internal receiving aperture (its outer envelope is larger), which sets the minimum clear diameter.
The cryogenic RF chain carries 1.2-1.8 GHz.
Optional: cooling is by a Gifford-McMahon cold head and helium compressor (no liquid cryogen), as required for a telescope-mounted receiver.
